conditions: x is any finite real number, including zero; ln is the real logarithm.
An explicit exact antiderivative differentiable on the entire real axis is required, up to one global additive constant.
The logarithmic substitution ln(1+x^2) is not injective on the real axis and has a stationary point at zero; neither fact permits excluding zero or choosing unrelated constants on the two half-axes.
x is real with x<-1 or x>1; these are exactly the real-domain components of the integrand. sqrt is the positive real square root on these components.
ln is the real logarithm, abs is real absolute value, and atan is the principal real inverse tangent.

An explicit exact antiderivative is required on both components, with an independent additive constant allowed on each. The points -1 and 1 are excluded; their one-sided primitive limits do not extend the original integrand's domain.
